story.title: Story 3: Archive Read and Reopen Surface

result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 3 against the story, tech design, and test plan, then inspected the Fastify archive route/schema, archive read service, Convex archive read path, client archive bootstrap/rendering, and the mapped Story 3 tests plus the configured story gate.

newFindings.title: The real Convex archive read path still loads the full archive before paginating
newFindings.evidence: Story 3 scope requires 'one bounded archive page' (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/07--archive-and-derived-views/stories/03-archive-read-and-reopen-surface.md:24-29`) and Flow 3 says `ArchiveReadService` fetches one bounded page from Convex (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/07--archive-and-derived-views/tech-design.md:604-608`). The production query behind that path does not stay bounded: `convex/archiveEntries.ts:139-154` calls `.collect()` on every matching `archiveEntries` row and only slices afterward in `paginateArchiveEntries`. Small-fixture tests still pass (`convex/archiveEntries.test.ts:407-435`, `tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts:123-282`), but long-lived processes will force a full archive read on every request, which breaks the intended bounded production read behavior.

gatesRun.command: corepack pnpm exec vitest run tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts tests/service/client/archive-section.test.ts

productionPathFindings: `convex/archiveEntries.ts:139-154` uses `.collect()` across the full process archive before pagination, so the real production read path is not actually bounded even though the API contract is.
additionalObservations: No fake adapter, shim, or placeholder branch was found in the archive Fastify/client runtime surface; the blocker is in the real Convex read path.
The Story 3 route/UI tests and `green-verify` gate pass because they exercise small fixtures and the in-memory store, so they do not expose the unbounded Convex query behavior.
